facts.t: Appears in 0.07% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (16 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 10).
In our 23,781-painting archive it is rarer than 70% of the named colors.
Inside a painting it most often plays a light (90% of the 10 paintings, by lightness rank within each painting, so varnish cannot fake it).

First seen in our archive in 1452 (commons-Q21729770, by Bartolomeo Caporali); the third-earliest painting is 1641, and the latest 1922 (10 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. That is 503 years before the name's earliest record in our sources (1955): the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment or dye.
In printed English the word peaks in the 1940s and rose fastest in the 1990s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
